text:
jade: FYI hit a nasty production case where retries + streaming body + auth refresh cause double-creates. The server uses X-Idempotency-Key to dedupe.

jade: Flow: stream upload -> first attempt 500 (transient) -> RetryPolicy rebuilds request -> header factory creates a fresh X-Idempotency-Key and the request body iterator is exhausted so the client re-reads from disk, resulting in two different ids and two creates.

rupert: Oof. Two distinct issues: 1) header factory being invoked per retry (we should preserve headers) 2) request body rewind semantics for iterables/async iterables. We currently don't provide a rewind interface so retries just re-open the file in callers' code sometimes which is error-prone.

elaine: Confirmed: our Request.build() runs header factories unconditionally. For streaming paths we call `await prepare_request()` on each attempt which re-runs header hooks. Bad for ephemeral headers like idempotency keys.

mike: I hit this earlier with chunked uploads where callers saw partial duplicates. My proposal: add RetryState.original_headers captured on first attempt and use those for subsequent attempts unless RetryOptions.allow_header_refresh==True. Default to preserve.

jade: For bodies we can add an interface `BodyRewindable` with `rewind()` that adapters can implement (file, io.BytesIO, custom generator wrappers). Retry logic will call rewind() before re-sending. If absent, fallback is to fail-fast with error asking caller to provide rewindable body.

rupert: Good. Also: what about Authorization header? If token expired we still need to refresh auth before retry. We should merge refreshed auth into preserved headers (override Authorization), not regenerate idempotency.

elaine: Agree. Implementation notes: capture original_headers = dict(request.headers) on attempt 0. On retry: request.headers = {**original_headers, **auth_refresh_headers, **user_overrides}. That preserves X-Idempotency-Key.

mike: Backoff: current exponential is too synchronized. Suggest switch default to "decorrelated jitter" (see aws / ex exponential backoff jitter patterns). Add tuning options: base, cap, jitter_factor.

jade: Typing/SDK surface: AsyncClient.request currently returns Union[Response, AsyncIterator[bytes]] via overloads and mypy is unhappy. We should split into explicit methods: `request()` -> Response or raise if streaming; `stream()` -> AsyncIterator[bytes]. Add generics for typed bodies: Response[T]. Update stubs.

rupert: Tests: create integration test harness that simulates: server returns 500 on first, 401 during same window to force auth refresh, then 201; assert server receives one create with same X-Idempotency-Key. Param both sync/async and streaming vs buffered.

typebot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/3201 (title: "preserve idempotency headers and rewindable bodies on retry")

mike: Small UX note: docs should show how to opt-out: `Client(retry=RetryOptions(allow_header_refresh=True))` and example for providing a rewindable body: `with open('large.bin','rb') as f: resp = client.post('/upload', data=RewindableFile(f))`.

elaine: I'll own typing stubs + docs. mike can own RetryState changes. jade can do body rewind interface + tests. rupert will review PR.

jade: I'll open PR with changelog note about potential behavioral change (headers preserved on retry). Link to issue in PR.

rupert: Thanks team. Small follow-up: consider a lint rule to detect header factories that return non-deterministic values to avoid surprises.

jade: Good idea. We'll add a mention in code-review checklist.
